idiom_name: ES class + #private elements, one concept per module
implementation_notes: An ES class with #private fields gives language-enforced privacy inside a single declaration, and one concept per module keeps the seam visible to importers; unlike WeakMap or underscore emulations, private elements cannot be reached or proxied from outside. Prefer it when the concept has identity, many instances and controlled mutation, and when subclassing is part of the design.
pitfalls: #private elements are invisible to JSON.stringify, spread and proxies, so persistence and DTO mapping need explicit accessors.
Passing a method as a callback loses this unless it is bound; arrow-function fields fix the binding but blur which members are part of the concept's API.

variants.name: Module-scoped factory function over closure state (ES2015)
variants.idiom_name: ES module + factory closure returning the concept's API object
variants.implementation_notes: The module file is the contour and everything not exported is private to it; a factory function closes over the concept's state and returns the operations as a plain object, so each instance gets its own scope and no this is involved. Choose it when the concept is created per request or per test and when a small frozen API object is more useful than a class hierarchy.
pitfalls: Closure state is unreachable from outside, so serialization needs an explicit toJSON/state export rather than reflection over the object.
There is no prototype and no instanceof relationship: brand checks or duck typing are required, and per-instance closures allocate one function set per object.
